title: Block structure and pairing
content: An AFSIM scenario is made of blocks: platform_type, platform, route, event_output, script_variables and so on. Each one closes with end_ plus the same keyword, such as end_platform or end_route. Pairing has nothing to do with indentation, and a missing close is reported at the end of the file.

title: A platform type is a closed namespace
content: The platform_type a platform instance references must really be defined in this file or somewhere along the include chain; it cannot be invented from the name. Referencing one that does not exist reports: Could not find platform_type xxx. When generating, use only the type names the knowledge list holds.

title: position order: latitude first
content: position takes latitude, then longitude, then an optional altitude; a coordinate reads DD:MM:SS.SSn DD:MM:SS.SSw, with the direction letter n/s/e/w attached to the number. Writing longitude first, in the GIS habit, reports: Bad value for: position, with exit code 1.

title: Waypoints must not repeat
content: Two adjacent route waypoints with identical coordinates stop the engine outright: Coincident waypoints!. Each waypoint reads position latitude longitude altitude XX ft msl speed XXX ft/s. When the requirement gives an altitude but no route, keep the endpoints at least 0.1 degree apart.

title: Every platform needs a side
content: A platform block must carry side blue or side red. With no side the platform becomes a neutral: nothing is reported, but it takes no part in detection or engagement, and its Side field in the event stream comes out empty.

title: event_output must enable events explicitly
content: With no enable list the contents of the event stream are not guaranteed: the smallest measured scenario produced a 69-byte .evt, and one with an include chain produced zero bytes. Enable every event class you need explicitly: PLATFORM_ADDED, PLATFORM_KILLED, WEAPON_FIRED, WEAPON_HIT. Once any enable is present, classes you did not list stop being written.

title: Globals must precede the includes
content: Top-level script_variables must come before every include_once. An include is textual pasting: the included script references the variable where it is expanded, so a declaration written later reports: Unknown identifier.

title: Units and number formats
content: AFSIM has no microsec unit; a one-microsecond pulse width is written 1.0e-6 sec. Numbers carry no thousands separator: altitude 30000 ft, not 30,000 ft. Time is in sec, speed in ft/s or m/sec.

title: A platform position takes no speed
content: The speed clause belongs to a route waypoint. Writing speed on a position line inside a platform block reports: Unknown command: speed. Initial speed can only be set through the speed of the route's first waypoint.

title: Write end_time explicitly
content: A scenario with no end_time runs 60 seconds by default; it does not run until the events stop. Write end_time 600 sec explicitly. Exit code 0 and complete in the log do not prove that an engagement happened: also check the event count in the .evt.

title: Altitude magnitude has to make sense
content: Altitude is in ft or m and its magnitude must match the requirement: a fighter is usually between 5000 and 40000 ft. Writing 30000 ft as altitude 3.0 ft raises no error, but the aircraft flies at ground level, sensor range collapses and nothing ever engages. Check every magnitude after generation.

title: Smallest flyable platform type
content: The smallest platform type for a self-contained scenario: platform_type NAME WSF_PLATFORM containing mover WSF_AIR_MOVER with maximum_speed 250 m/sec, closed with end_mover and end_platform_type. A platform instance then references the type and supplies side and position.

title: Error keywords at a glance
content: Bad value for: means a number or a coordinate failed to parse, usually because of coordinate order, a unit or a thousands separator. Unknown command: means the block holds a command that does not exist there. Unknown identifier: means a variable is undeclared, or declared too late. Could not find platform_type means the type name does not exist. Unexpected End Of Data means a block was not closed.

title: Two ways to write a route
content: A route can be a top-level block that a platform references, or written inline inside the platform block as position waypoints. Both forms require paired coordinates, no duplicates, and both altitude and speed.
